# statmesh

> Open public statistics behind one query surface. Search series from many official sources
> (World Bank, IMF, OECD, ILOSTAT, Eurostat, ECB, BIS, UN SDG, FAOSTAT, UN Comtrade, SEC EDGAR,
> GLEIF, Census, FRED and more), read observations, join across sources on country, year, HS
> product or company, and run read-only SQL. Every number comes with its source, licence and
> retrieval time.

Use statmesh for questions about public statistics. Do not answer such questions from memory.

## Citation rules

- Every result carries `citations[]`. Quote them with each number: source, licence, retrieval time.
- Quote the attribution string when a series has one.
- Do not state a number that no tool result contains. Flag any figure you cannot trace to a result.
- `redistribute` is `yes`, `review` or `no`. On the hosted mirror only `yes` data is served.
  Say so when a licence limits reuse.

## When data is missing

When no result holds the number the user asked for:

1. Say what you searched (query, filters, source).
2. Show the 3 closest series and how each differs from what was asked (geography, period,
   unit, age or sex breakdown, frequency).
3. Name the source that would hold the data, even if statmesh does not have it yet.
4. Do not give a number from memory in its place.

## Paging and flags

- Search and observations take `offset`. Pass `next_offset` as the next `offset` until it is null.
- Search pages through its first 2000 results. `offset + limit` past 2000 is an error (HTTP 422 on
  REST): narrow the query instead.
- Observations: `truncated: true` means more rows follow at `next_offset`. `partial: true` means the
  dataset itself is partial because a row cap cut its ingest or on-demand fetch; say so with each
  number from it.

## MCP tools

Stdio (`statmesh mcp`) or HTTP at `/mcp`.

- `search_series(q, geo, freq, source, topic, start_year, end_year, updated_since, redistribute, limit, offset)`:
  keyword search over the catalog. Filters combine. `q` may be empty when a filter is set. `geo` is a
  code, an ISO alpha-2 or a name (India, World), or a comma list (series must cover all; ids then have
  no geo suffix); an unknown geo is an error.
- `describe_series(series_id)`: metadata, dimensions, licence and citation of one series.
- `get_observations(series_id, start, end, geo, limit, filters, offset, compact)`: observations. `geo` takes
  a code, an ISO alpha-2 or a country name. Without `limit` you get at most 200 rows, the latest
  periods of every geo (`200 // n_geos` each; over 200 geos only the first 200 show);
  `omitted_rows` and `warning` say what was cut; `offset` needs `limit`. `compact` (default true) returns `columns` + array `rows`
  with same-on-every-row columns under `constants`; `compact=false` is the full shape. Remote series
  are fetched on demand and may be rate limited. `filters` are connector filters, for example
  `{"partner": "USA", "hs": "85"}`.
- `list_sources(q, kind, topic, redistribute, auth, status)`: sources with freshness and key status.
- `describe_schema()`: every SQL view with columns, types, examples and join hints.
- `run_sql(sql)`: one read-only SELECT over those views.
- `run_python(code)`: only when the sandbox is enabled. No network.

## REST endpoints

Base URL: the server root (`http://127.0.0.1:8000` locally). Interactive docs: `/docs`.
Machine-readable spec: `/openapi.json`. On the hosted mirror the whole REST API lives under `/v1`
(for example `/v1/search` and `/v1/openapi.json`); the MCP endpoint stays at `/mcp`.

- `GET /search?q=...&source=&topic=&geo=&freq=&start_year=&end_year=&limit=&offset=`
- `GET /sources`
- `GET /schema`
- `POST /query` with body `{"sql": "SELECT ..."}`
- `GET /series/{series_id}`: metadata and citation
- `GET /series/{series_id}/observations?start=&end=&geo=&limit=&offset=&filter=key=value`
- `GET /series/{series_id}/observations.csv`: streamed CSV, row cap in `X-Statmesh-Row-Cap`
- `POST /shares` and `GET /shares/{id}`: public read-only answer links
- `GET /healthz`
- `POST /python`: only when the sandbox is enabled

Series ids look like `source:dataset:indicator:geo`, for example
`ilostat:DF_UNE_DEAP_SEX_AGE_RT:UNE_DEAP_RT:IND`.

## Example

Question: unemployment rate in India since 2015.

1. `search_series(q="unemployment India", freq="A")`
2. `get_observations(series_id="ilostat:DF_UNE_DEAP_SEX_AGE_RT:UNE_DEAP_RT:IND", start="2015-01-01")`
3. Answer with the values, quoting the ILOSTAT citation (licence CC BY 4.0, retrieval time).

## Setup guides

Client setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and ChatGPT: `docs/ai-apps.md` in the repository.
